correctionsFoundByTheUnfilteredRun.cause: Three cases of the fixture share one saga repository and two of them used the service name A. The retry case left an instance in the running state, so the neighbouring case sent its start into that instance instead of creating one.
correctionsFoundByTheUnfilteredRun.correction: The retry case uses its own service name, exactly as the third case of the fixture already did.
correctionsFoundByTheUnfilteredRun.probe: Restoring the shared name turns the fixture red again.

correctionsFoundByTheUnfilteredRun.symptom: TaskCanceledException after 30 seconds in the unfiltered run
correctionsFoundByTheUnfilteredRun.cause: The case is named after a retry it never performed. Its status message reached the endpoint before the saga existed, and an uncorrelated event of this state machine was dropped instead of faulted, so there was nothing to retry. It passed only when the ordering happened to be favourable.
correctionsFoundByTheUnfilteredRun.measurement: Forcing the adverse ordering reproduced the timeout deterministically. Adding a retry policy alone did not help, which proved the message was never faulted.
correctionsFoundByTheUnfilteredRun.correction: The status event of the fixture state machine faults on a missing instance and the endpoint retries. The case now waits for the first retry as an event instead of sleeping, and asserts that the retry happened at all.
correctionsFoundByTheUnfilteredRun.probe: Removing the missing instance policy turns the case red again.
correctionsFoundByTheUnfilteredRun.scope: test only, inside the fixture and its own state machine
